checklistText: Ghosting on foliage and moving elements: doubled or semi-transparent edges where something moved between brackets (AutoHDR QC checklist, Oct 13 2026)

escalateTo.when: the ghosting is on the primary or hero exterior, or covers a large, obvious part of the frame

deescalateTo.when: a small, peripheral ghost a viewer is unlikely to notice

visionHint: Check all greenery, branches, flags, water, and any car or person seen through windows for doubled, semi-transparent or smeared edges left by movement between bracketed frames. Do not flag natural motion blur in a water feature, depth-of-field softness, or reflections.

checklistText: Test shots, misfires and accidental captures in the delivery set (AutoHDR QC checklist, Oct 13 2026)

escalateTo.when: the frame is unusable: mostly black or white, lens cap, floor or ceiling only, or the photographer's hand or feet

visionHint: Flag frames that are clearly not deliverable: a lens cap or blank exposure, a shot of the floor, ceiling or sky by accident, a settings or color-card test, the photographer's hand or feet, or a frame cut mid-movement. The fix is to exclude the photo from delivery. Do not flag an intentional detail or close-up shot.

sectionName: Reflections, Dust, Glare, and Unwanted Objects
checklistText: Drone visible in windows, glass, mirrors or other reflections (AutoHDR QC checklist, Oct 13 2026)

deescalateTo.when: a tiny, distant speck that is only identifiable on close inspection

reeditPromptTemplate: Remove the drone reflected in the {location}. Keep the glass, frame and reflection of the scene unchanged. Change nothing else in the photo.
visionHint: Look for a drone (a small quadcopter shape, often with visible rotors) reflected in windows, glass doors, pools, car paint or other shiny surfaces, especially in aerial and exterior photos. Do not flag birds, insects or distant aircraft in the sky.
